paper_metadata.title: Heterostructure-enabled creep resistance and deformation mechanisms in a new Ni-Co-based high-entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The present alloy shows a superior low steady creep rate of 0.00044%/h. Transmission elec- tron microscopy revealed a progressive transition in deformation mechanisms during creep: from disloca- tion climb and stacking fault activity in the matrix to γ′precipitate shearing dominated by APBs and SISFs. These findings highlight the critical role of heterostruc- tural design in enhancing both strength and creep resis- tance and provide valuable insights for the development of next-generation Ni-Co-based superalloys for high- temperature disk applications.

Simultaneously, the embrittlement of the equiaxed HEA at a creep temperature of 725 °C upon stress of 630MPa can be defeated in its heterogeneous counterpart. The present alloy shows a superior low steady creep rate of 0.00044%/h.
